title: Oklahoma and Texas Tech Set the FBS Yardage Record in 2016
question: What is the FBS record for combined yards in a game, and did Oklahoma play in it?
answer: Oklahoma's 66-59 win at Texas Tech on October 22, 2016, produced 1,708 combined yards, an FBS record at the time. Each team finished with 854 yards, topping the 1,640 San Jose State and Nevada totaled in 2001.
summary: Oklahoma beat Texas Tech 66-59 in 2016 in a game that produced an FBS-record 1,708 combined yards, with 854 for each team. Here is how it happened.
body: On Saturday, October 22, 2016, Oklahoma traveled to Lubbock and walked into one of the wildest scoreboards in college football history. The Sooners won 66-59, and the two offenses together piled up 1,708 yards, which was reported as the most ever in an FBS game.
The numbers split evenly: Oklahoma gained 854 yards and Texas Tech gained 854 yards. The previous combined mark, 1,640 yards, had stood since San Jose State and Nevada met in 2001.

Baker Mayfield, back in the stadium where his college career began, threw for 545 yards and a then-school-record seven touchdowns for the Sooners. Joe Mixon became the first Oklahoma player with 200 rushing yards and 100 receiving yards in the same game, and the reports cited here put his touchdown total at five.

Across the field, Texas Tech quarterback Patrick Mahomes II finished with 819 total yards, an FBS single-game record, and 734 passing yards, which tied Washington State's Connor Halliday for the passing mark. Sooner fans often remember this one as the day a defense was optional.
Note that outlets disagreed on small details such as Mixon's exact rushing total and first-down counts, so this post sticks to the figures that the sources consistently report.
